We’re building a relationship-oriented bank for the modern world. We need talented, passionate professionals who are dedicated to doing what’s right for our clients.
At CIBC, we embrace your strengths and your ambitions, so you are empowered at work. Our team members have what they need to make a meaningful impact and are truly valued for who they are and what they contribute.
To learn more about CIBC, please visit CIBC.com
What you'll be doing

When you become a Commercial Banking Associate, you will be joining a team that for more than a century has been helping businesses reach their full potential. Through a structured and comprehensive training program that includes classroom and on-the-job training, you will have the opportunity to learn how to deliver flexible business solutions and provide dedicated and timely business expertise to help clients realize their goals.

The Commercial Banking team supports our account teams through client acquisition, relationship management as well as transactional support for client-specific financing solutions. As an associate on the team, you will have an opportunity to learn the products, processes, networks and functions to enable and equip you to eventually progress to the Relationship Manager role and oversee your own portfolio of clients.

As a Commercial Banking Associate, you will be assisting our Commercial Banking Managers with their existing clients relationships as well as new financing transactions by providing quality financial and industry analysis as part of the deal team. You will also participate in all activities through the sales cycle in order to prepare you for the Relationship Manager role. You’ll have a chance to assist with business development initiatives with a focus on meeting growth targets. This means that you will work in identifying business opportunities and financing solutions to meet the needs of the client.

You’ll begin your journey with Orientation Activities to help you get acclimated to the team and role and will equip you with the skills and knowledge to provide the best possible experience to CIBC clients – we know there’s a learning curve and we’re here to help.

It’s hands-on, so you’ll get the real-life experience you need to rise to the challenge.

As an Associate you'll complete a number of training sessions related directly to the role including credit structuring, risk assessment, and cash management. You will have ongoing coaching and mentoring by your leaders and will be supported by a Program Manager who will lead virtual learning sessions, host touchpoints and guide Associates through this structured program. You’ll have an opportunity to develop a number of soft skills including business development, negotiation and networking.

Important information:
You must be in your final year of post-secondary education pursuing a degree/diploma in Business, Finance, Accounting, or related fields with an expected graduation date before May 31st, 2027.
Applications should include your resume (no more than 2 pages) and cover letter (no more than 1 page) and academic transcript uploaded as 1 document to the “Resume/CV section” of the application
Work location: Atlantic region (Nova Scotia and New Brunswick). Exact city of work location will be confirmed later during the interview process taking into account the selected candidates’ preference. Mobility is an asset.

At CIBC we enable the work environment most optimal for you to thrive in your role. Details on your work arrangement (proportion of on-site and remote work) will be discussed at the time of your interview.

How you'll succeed
Client Engagement - Connect on a personal level to make every interaction meaningful. Enhance relationships by collaborating with your team and providing administrative support to ensure client needs are met. Respond to requests by answering questions and providing an exceptional experience.
Relationship Building - Heighten CIBC brand awareness in your community by attending local events and participating in marketing and outreach activities. Grow your network to create lasting connections that will generate future opportunities. Work closely with your team to connect clients with the right opportunities.
Research & evaluation – Assist in evaluating business growth opportunities through comprehensive industry, client and prospect research. Prepare analyses in support of credit submissions including structuring and documentation.
Innovation - Make an impact by assisting in problem solving and finding solution and often going above and beyond in assisting to find a resolution.

Who you are
You can demonstrate experience in the field. You understand financial statements and accounting principles includes valuation techniques and cash flow analysis. If you have a knowledge of commercial banking products and service offerings, that would be asset.
You give meaning to data. Research is your thing! You enjoy analyzing business growth opportunities through comprehensive industry, client and prospect research. You also like taking that analysis and organizing it into support of credit submissions including structuring and documentation
You’re passionate about people. You enjoy building relationships by making an impact on your community and showing clients they’re appreciated by engaging in marketing and outreach activities. You’ve been able to develop new relationships by getting referrals from existing relationships and centers of influence. You’re a skilled communicator (written and spoken): You’re open to ideas and concepts presented by others. You actively listen to ensure that you’ve understood direction and grasped new information. You genuinely enjoy engaging with co-workers to get work done. You’re motivated by collective success. You enjoy collaborating with a team to come up with innovative solutions to a problem that will make a difference today and tomorrow. You also provide guidance on treasury best practices and cash management solutions that will best meet your clients’ needs.
You put our clients first. You consistently put the client first by proactively assessing your clients’ needs and proposing solutions to meet those needs. Your understanding of business and financial concepts allows you to provide “best in class” service and client/prospect proposals for financial and strategic solutions to meet client needs. You’re goal oriented. You are focused on meeting your goals and delivering your best efforts to make an impact on the client and the team.
You live your values. You bring high standards, genuine care to your relationships, and want to grow with an employer that shares your values and brings out your best.
What CIBC Offers
At CIBC, your goals are a priority. We start with your strengths and ambitions as an employee and strive to create opportunities to tap into your potential. We aspire to give you a career, rather than just a paycheck.
We work to recognize you in meaningful, personalized ways including a competitive salary, incentive pay, banking benefits, a benefits program*, defined benefit pension plan*, an employee share purchase plan, a vacation offering, wellbeing support, and MomentMakers, our social, points-based recognition program.
Our spaces and technological toolkit will make it simple to bring together great minds to create innovative solutions that make a difference for our clients.
We cultivate a culture where you can express your ambition through initiatives like Purpose Day; a paid day off dedicated for you to use to invest in your growth and development.
*Subject to plan and program terms and conditions
What you need to know
CIBC is committed to creating an inclusive environment where all team members and clients feel like they belong. We seek applicants with a wide range of abilities and we provide an accessible candidate experience. If you need accommodation, please contact Mailbox.careers-carrieres@cibc.com
CIBC is committed to clarity in our hiring process. All roles posted are opportunities we’re actively recruiting for, unless stated otherwise.

We may ask you to complete an attribute-based assessment and other skills test (such as simulation, coding, French proficiency).
We use artificial intelligence tools during the recruitment process. Our goal for the application process is to get to know more about you, all that you have to offer, and give you the opportunity to learn more about us.

Manulife / John Hancock is seeking a highly skilled Full-Stack Data Engineer, Modernization & Migration to join our Insurance Licensing & Compensation Engineering team.
The successful candidate will play a key role in the migration of legacy licensing & compensation capabilities to vendor Platform & Data Lake.

This role will focus on analyzing and transforming complex legacy data, building scalable ETL/ELT pipelines, supporting data conversion and reconciliation, and developing the reports, extracts, and downstream feeds required to enable the future-state platform.

The ideal candidate combines strong SQL, Informatica/ADF/Data Bricks, data warehousing, data modeling, ETL, reporting, and data analysis skills with the ability to understand complex business rules and data relationships across legacy and modern platforms.

Position Responsibilities:
Analyze data structures, relationships, transformations, and business rules across multiple legacy systems, and related upstream and downstream platforms.
Design and develop ETL/ELT pipelines using Informatica, Azure Data Factory (ADF), SQL, or Databricks to support data conversion, integration, and downstream delivery.
Support the migration and conversion of data into the target compensation platform and the Data Lake.
Perform source-to-target mapping, data profiling, cleansing, transformation, validation, and reconciliation throughout the migration lifecycle.
Design and maintain 3NF, dimensional, and analytical data models supporting business processing, reporting, reconciliation, and downstream consumption.
Build automated data extracts, interfaces, and feeds for Finance, Distribution, Operations, Treasury, and other enterprise consumers.
Develop operational, reconciliation, and analytical reporting using tools such as Power BI, Tableau, Cognos, SSRS, or Crystal Reports.
Develop automated controls to validate record counts, financial totals, balances, results, and source-to-target completeness.
Partner with business analysts, engineers, architects, and Operations to translate legacy data structures and processing requirements into future-state solutions.
Investigate complex data issues across source systems, transformation layers, target vendor platform, and downstream consumers and support root-cause analysis and remediation.
Build and maintain scheduling, monitoring, alerting, restart, and exception-handling capabilities for production data pipelines.
Maintain clear data lineage, mappings, transformation rules, technical specifications, and reconciliation evidence to support auditability and production readiness.
Contribute to migration planning, test-data preparation, conversion rehearsals, parallel validation, cutover, and post-production stabilization.

Required Qualifications:
Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Software Engineering, Data Engineering, or a related field, or equivalent professional experience.
4+ years of experience in data engineering, ETL development, data migration, Cloud data engineering.
Advanced SQL skills with experience analyzing and transforming large and complex datasets.
Strong hands-on experience with Informatica, Azure Data Factory (ADF), Data Bricks or comparable ETL/ELT platforms.
Strong working knowledge of data warehousing, 3NF, Medallion Architecture, dimensional modeling, and enterprise data-model design.
Work experience with large-scale data migration or system-conversion initiatives, including source-to-target mapping, profiling, transformation, validation, and reconciliation.
Experience building automated extracts and file-based integrations, including CSV, TSV, XML, JSON, or similar formats.

Role Summary
We are seeking a Third Party Risk Senior Analyst to support the organization’s Third-Party Risk Management (TPRM) program. This role is responsible for assessing, challenging, and monitoring third-party risks throughout the vendor lifecycle, ensuring alignment with internal policies, regulatory expectations, and the organization’s risk appetite.
A key responsibility of this role is to provide effective challenge of Inherent Risk Questionnaires (IRQs) to ensure the information provided by Contract Owners and business stakeholders is accurate, complete, internally consistent, and appropriately reflects the nature and risk of the third-party engagement. The resulting inherent risk assessment determines the scope and level of due diligence and ongoing monitoring required for the third party.
The ideal candidate will have experience in third-party risk management, operational risk, compliance, or audit, with practical experience conducting inherent risk assessments, financial and adverse media reviews, ongoing monitoring, and governance activities.

Key Responsibilities
Risk Assessment & Due Diligence
· Conduct and provide effective challenge of Inherent Risk Questionnaires (IRQs) completed by Contract Owners and business stakeholders, assessing whether responses are accurate, complete, internally consistent, and appropriately reflect the nature of the supplier engagement.
· Challenge responses where information appears incomplete, inconsistent, or does not appropriately reflect factors such as service criticality, data sensitivity, technology dependencies, regulatory impact, or other relevant risk considerations.
· Ensure the IRQ appropriately identifies the supplier’s inherent risk, as this assessment determines the scope and level of required due diligence and ongoing monitoring.
· Escalate material gaps, inconsistencies, or unresolved concerns before the inherent risk assessment is finalized.
· Perform financial due diligence, including review of supplier financial health, financial risk indicators, and credit information.
· Conduct adverse/negative media reviews to identify potential reputational, legal, regulatory, or operational concerns.
· Assess supplier risk information and identify areas requiring additional due diligence, escalation, or risk mitigation.
· Review relevant third-party risk documentation and supporting evidence to assess completeness and identify potential risk concerns.
· Provide guidance to Contract Owners and business stakeholders on TPRM requirements and their responsibilities throughout the vendor lifecycle.

Ongoing Monitoring & Governance
· Conduct risk-based ongoing monitoring of third parties in accordance with established policies, standards, and monitoring requirements.
· Monitor supplier risk indicators, including financial health and performance, adverse/negative media, emerging global risks, and material changes to the supplier or services provided.
· Assess changes in supplier risk and determine whether additional review, escalation, or risk mitigation is required.
· Support periodic supplier reviews and maintain clear documentation of the supplier’s current risk posture.
· Track risk findings, issues, remediation actions, and policy exceptions through resolution.
· Identify and escalate material changes in supplier risk in accordance with established governance requirements.

· Support Contract Owners in understanding their accountability for ongoing supplier risk management.

Compliance & Audit Support

· Support Contract Owners in understanding and fulfilling their accountability for third-party risk throughout the vendor lifecycle.

Program Support & Continuous Improvement

· Support the preparation of risk reporting, dashboards, metrics, and governance materials.
· Identify opportunities to improve data quality, risk assessment effectiveness, process efficiency, and risk oversight.
· Support improvements to inherent risk assessment and ongoing monitoring processes.
· Stay informed of emerging third-party risks, regulatory developments, industry practices, and technology-related risks.

· 2–5 years of relevant experience in one or more of the following:
· Third-Party Risk Management / Vendor Risk Management
· Compliance

· Technology or Information Risk
· Experience conducting or supporting:
· Inherent risk assessments and effective challenge of risk questionnaires
· Third-party due diligence
· Financial risk reviews
· Adverse/negative media reviews
· Ongoing supplier monitoring
· Issue and remediation tracking
· Strong understanding of the third-party lifecycle, including onboarding, risk assessment, due diligence, ongoing monitoring, governance, and offboarding.
· Understanding of risk-based assessment and monitoring methodologies.
· Demonstrated ability to critically evaluate information, identify inconsistencies or gaps, and appropriately challenge risk assessments and supporting information.
· Familiarity with third-party risk regulatory expectations, including OSFI Guideline B-10 or comparable regulatory requirements, is an asset.

· Strong risk assessment and analytical skills
· Effective challenge and critical-thinking capabilities
· Sound judgment and the ability to identify and escalate material risk concerns
· Strong attention to detail and documentation discipline

· Ability to analyze information from multiple sources and develop a clear risk view
· Ability to manage multiple assessments and priorities
· Training and facilitation skills

Preferred Qualifications
